name: Trincomalee
line: A deep harbour, calm water and empty beaches when the south is wet.

image.alt: A long, quiet beach with clear water and palms

summary: A deep natural harbour on the north east coast, with calm water and empty beaches in the months the south is wet.

intro.heading: The other coast.
paragraphs: Trincomalee has one of the largest natural harbours in the world, and a small, busy town around it. North of the town, the beaches at Uppuveli and Nilaveli run for miles, with warm, shallow water and very few people.

From May to September, while the south west monsoon soaks the other coast, the sea here is flat and clear. That is when we send people east: to swim, to snorkel off Pigeon Island, and to go out looking for whales and dolphins.

mapCaption: On the north east coast. The other dots are the places we pair it with.

doing.lede: Trincomalee is for the months the south is wet. These are the things we build the days around.

items.title: Snorkelling at Pigeon Island
items.body: A small marine park off Nilaveli, with reef, turtles and blacktip reef sharks in shallow water. Go early, before the boats.

items.title: Koneswaram temple
items.body: A Hindu temple on Swami Rock, high above the sea at the end of the old fort. The view is as much the reason to go as the shrine.

items.title: Whales and dolphins
items.body: Blue whales pass close to this coast from around March to August, and dolphins are about for most of the season.

items.title: Nilaveli beach
items.body: Miles of soft sand and warm water with almost nobody on it. The best swimming on the island in July.

season: The east coast runs the other way to the south: calm and dry from May to September, and wet while the north east monsoon blows from November to January. It is the answer to a summer trip.
ctaBody: Tell us your dates. If they fall in the summer, we will build the route around this coast.
